body: I have experienced some similar behavior, but haven't been able to track this down specificially. @lsmith77 also has reported something to that effect IIRC.

On 28.07.2011, at 11:09, schmittjoh reply@reply.github.com wrote:

> I have experienced some similar behavior, but haven't been able to track this down specificially. @lsmith77 also has reported something to that effect IIRC.

yes. its quite strange. the other way to fix it is to add an exit() call after send() in the front controller. i briefly tried to figure out if its related to output buffering, but couldnt determine a cause.
Does adding a flush() solve it too?

Its strange. Testing inside firefox it only seems to help to do a die(), using another client a flush() does seem to do the trick. But things get even stranger as this issue only happens with some urls in my application. I tried shift reloading and everything. Right now I am basically totally at a loss as to what is causing this making my report somewhat useless.

After updating to stable at last, I noticed the same issue here. You can try it with firebug in the Net tab: http://nelm.io/ has the onload in ~500ms, http://nelm.io/?cl=1 (that re-enables the content-length header) takes 15seconds for the browser to time out. It's waiting for 9K to come, but gzipped content is only 2.7K. 

I'd recommend removing the header, unless that causes issue anywhere, in which case I really don't know what we'll do :)

BTW this was with Apache 2.2 + mod_fastcgi, according to stuff I read, _maybe_ mod_fcgid wouldn't cause the issue, but I don't consider this an acceptable fix, and it seems like @krevindiou has had it with IIS too anyway.

> http://nelm.io/?cl=1

I'm not experiencing this issue in chrome at that URL.

Well, obviously every browser has its own way of coping, but the fact is this is not a valid HTTP response anymore.

Besides, sending the Content-Length seems to remove Apache's ability to send `Transfer-Encoding:chunked`, which is a bit fail too.

We need a content-length in the MultiCurlAsync client in Buzz:
https://github.com/liip/Buzz/blob/master/lib/Buzz/Client/MultiCurlAsync.php#L70

Then again I am sure there is likely a more reliable way to set the Content-Length via the web server ..?
BTW I am getting this issue on OSX with a more or less stock Apache

@lsmith77 Re: MultiCurlAsync, this is usually a special case and an optimization, so I think you can add the Content-Length yourself on the backend.

For the rest, the main issue is that if you have script behaviors that rely on the load event, they are delayed by 15seconds in some browsers, which is really unacceptable.

> My actual workaround is to comment this Content-Length setting.
> 
> Then again I am sure there is likely a more reliable way to set the Content-Length via the web server ..?

I would imagine if you just commented it out, the web server would set it.

@lsmith77: PR #1551 is where this addition has been added by @lenar. If nobody comes up with a good solution, I think we can just revert this change (and work on a more robust solution for 2.1). As I said in the referenced PR, this should be handled automatically by the web server anyway.

Not setting Content-Length removes the ability to do keep-alive automatically. In case of Apache + no mod_deflate in use
at least. Apache does not add Content-Length header by itself but only when it has mod_deflate enabled and that module decides to act on response content.

But I'm not against not setting the header if it introduces other problems (as it seems). Still I wouldn't revert the whole change just the setting of Content-Length: header. If that's ok, then I'll be happy to do the PR myself.
@lenar: We just need to remove the Content-Length header for now and work on a better solution (whatever what it means) for 2.1.
